newsitem.title: USA: Mitsubishi to use Molten Metal process.
newsitem.headline: Mitsubishi to use Molten Metal process.

text.p: M4 Environmental LP said Mitsubishi Corp has agreed to use Catalytic Extraction Processing as the principle technology for destroying chemical weapons left in China by the Japanese Army after World War II.

The Japanese government is studying alternative technologies for the demilitarization of their World War II era chemical weapons, M4 said. The company is a limited partnership of Lockheed Martin Corp and Molten Metal Technology Inc, which developed the CEP technology.

To assist in this effort, Mitsubishi has agreed with M4 to utilize a CEP-based system to destroy bulk agent and select weapons located at small weapons burial sites. Mitsubishi is the leading Japanese company being considered to spearhead the cleanup of Japanese chemical weapons left in China.
"Japan has just begun developing their chemical demilitarization program and is seeking new technologies for this work," said Robert Merriman, M4 chief executive officer.
